summary: Sustained request timeouts for multi-turn chat with deep conversation history and very high max_tokens
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports repeated request timeouts (HTTP 504 / streaming disconnect) when sending multi-turn conversations with very deep history (>= 25 messages) combined with max_tokens set above 12,000.
Impact: NovaHealth saw 15% of production inference requests fail for a subset of chat flows over a 3-hour window, causing degraded UX for clinicians and elevated support contacts.
Environment: Production (us-west-2), dedicated tenant on Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool), model pinned to redwood-v2-large.
Observed behavior: Requests initially stream tokens but often stall after ~60-120s and then terminate with 504 or client-side socket reset. Failures are most frequent when KV cache size grows large due to long conversation history and when customers set high max_tokens for final answer generation.
Frequency: Intermittent but reproducible for sessions with deep history and high max_tokens.
Customer impact note: Customer is on an enterprise contract with SLAs; business critical workflows (clinical summarization) were interrupted.
steps_to_reproduce: Create a long multi-turn chat session with ~30 prior messages (system + user + assistant).
Set generation parameters: model=redwood-v2-large, max_tokens=12500, temperature=0.2, streaming=true.
Issue the request to the /v1/chat/completions endpoint with the full history included as messages[].
Observe that streaming returns initial chunks, then stalls between 60-120s, and request either times out with 504 or the client connection resets.
Repeat with reduced history (<=10 messages) or reduced max_tokens (<=2048) and note the request completes successfully.

comments: [2026-03-10 15:05 UTC] Support (Aisha): Contacted customer, confirming impact and requested sample payloads and full request_id headers.

[2026-03-10 15:20 UTC] Customer (NovaHealth - product): Sent three failing request_ids and a sample session export (30 messages + system prompt + docs). Reports failures only when max_tokens above 10k.

[2026-03-10 16:00 UTC] SRE (Marco): Correlated request_ids in prod cluster; saw sustained finalizer queue growth and KV cache evictions during the window. Opened runtime investigation and increased observability sampling.

[2026-03-10 18:40 UTC] Runtime eng (Priya): Reproduced backlog locally when KV cache exceeded ~3.5GB. Hypothesis: large KV entries cause serialization/deserialization stalls under current kernel swap logic.

[2026-03-11 09:15 UTC] Support (Aisha): Provided customer with temporary mitigation steps (trim conversation history, reduce max_tokens to <4k, set prefer_fast_path=true). Customer applied mitigation and confirms requests complete.

[2026-03-12 12:30 UTC] Eng (Marco): Rolled out limited-rate patch to finalizer that prioritizes token emission for streaming and avoids large blocking serialization on critical path. Monitoring for regressions.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: network flakiness or API gateway idle timeouts — ruled out: other customers in same AZ not affected and gateway logs show healthy upstream connectivity.
Observed pattern: failures co-occur with high kv_cache_size and increased eviction rates; finalizer component shows GC/serialization pauses correlated with stalled streaming.
Repro locally: synthetic workload with 35 messages and max_tokens=12k reproduces ~60-90s stall on redwood-v2-large when using default kernel swap path.
Profiling: blocking syscall in kv-serialization routine while writing >2.5MB KV frames to temp storage; scheduler backlog increases and timeouts follow.
Grafana panels: contended finalizer threads (thread_cpu>85%), scheduler queue depth spike, p99 latency for token emission increases sharply.
Temporary mitigation verified: trimming history to reduce KV size avoids the stall; switching to model variant with smaller key/value footprint also avoids issue.

Related to recent runtime change: PR #3412 introduced a lazy-serialization optimization but has a path that falls back to blocking serialization for large KV blobs — likely trigger for these workloads.
Customer-specific: NovaHealth uses long structured system prompts + document snippets which inflate tokenized history size beyond typical chat loads.
root_cause: Blocking KV serialization path that performs synchronous writes for large KV blobs (triggered by very deep conversation history and high max_tokens), causing finalizer threads to stall and scheduler backlog to grow, resulting in request timeouts and streaming disconnects.
resolution: Implemented a hotfix that avoids blocking serialization on the streaming emission path: large KV blobs are now asynchronously checkpointed and finalizer is prioritized for active streaming requests. Hotfix rolled to affected us-west-2 Dedicated pool at 2026-03-12 03:20 UTC. Monitoring shows error rate dropped to baseline.
workaround:
1) Trim conversation history (remove older assistant turns) or summarize earlier context before sending.
2) Reduce max_tokens to <= 4096 for large-history sessions.
3) Temporarily pin to a model variant with smaller KV footprint.
4) Set prefer_fast_path=true to favor low-latency execution if available.
next_steps: Postmortem write-up and root-cause doc scheduled for 2026-03-15 (owner: Marco).
Backport async-serialization fix to stable branch and release to Dedicated clusters next week (owner: runtime team).
Add telemetry alert for kv_cache_size > 3GB + finalizer_queue_depth > 50 to catch regressions early.
Customer follow-up: schedule a sync with NovaHealth to review long-term guidance for handling deep-history workflows and offer migration assistance.
